slides.teacher_cue: New sound — long /uː/. Spelled oo. Lips round tightly, like blowing out a candle. Hold the sound — it is long. moon, food, cool, spoon. Note: oo has two sounds in English. Today is the long one: /uː/. The short one /ʊ/ (as in book, cook) comes in the next lesson.
slides.expected_response: Students produce long /uː/ cleanly with tight lip rounding and sustained length.
slides.correction_move: Model lip rounding — tighter than /oʊ/. Students hold the sound for two seconds. Contrast /oʊ/ (boat) with /uː/ (boot) — both have lip rounding but /uː/ is much tighter and higher.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /oʊ/ substitution — Korean learners may not fully round for /uː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect oo (long /uː/) to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say oo (long /uː/) clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Point up and say moon. oo in the middle. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say moon orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model moon orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for long /uː/ — tight lip rounding.

slides.teacher_cue: Say food — things we eat. Confirm /f/ onset and long /uː/. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say food orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model food orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /p/ on /f/ and for long /uː/ — not short.

slides.teacher_cue: Say cool — not warm; also excellent. Confirm /uː/ and /l/ coda. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say cool orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model cool orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ vs /r/ in coda and long /uː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Hold up a spoon. sp onset, oo vowel team. Reveal and blend all four sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students say spoon orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model spoon orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for sp onset — both consonants before the vowel — and long /uː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to a tooth. Confirm /uː/ and voiceless /θ/ at the end. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say tooth orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model tooth orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /t/ substitution on /θ/ at the end and for long /uː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say smooth — even, not rough. sm onset, oo vowel, voiced /ð/ at the end. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say smooth orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model smooth orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /d/ substitution on /ð/ at the end and for long /uː/.
